summary.intent: Execute Phase 41 (Package and App Versioning and Release Cycles) using wave-based parallel execution across 5 plans covering Release Please config, PR release preview, staging tag format, and batched releases.
summary.outcome: Waves 1 and 2 completed (plans 41-01, 41-02, 41-04). All three worktrees were merged into the feature branch after resolving lint errors and cherry-pick conflicts. Wave 3 (41-03) is next.

repo: The monorepo has 15 packages requiring independent versioning via release-please-config.json — root extra-files cascade was removed, desktop extra-files retained
release-please-manifest.json needs all 15 entries with correct initial versions
GitHub Actions scripts use Node 22 and trigger on PR events to main with release-please PR exclusion
The API and TEE service form a lock group (D-05) — they version together
Web and desktop packages use monotonic versioning rules (D-08, D-13)
Dependency cascade detection uses hardcoded JS_DEPS and RUST_DEPS graphs (D-21-24)
rootFolderKey migration is fully complete — dual-write window concern is outdated, DB crypto columns are dropped
BYO-IPFS auth token is implemented as encrypted IPNS entry; server stores only boolean isByoUser flag
Kubo is already at v0.40.0 in docker/docker-compose.yml — upgrade concern is outdated
Subfolder recovery is implemented but limited by IPNS DHT propagation — architectural, not a bug

code.finding: 746-line script with dead code: maxBump function was defined but never called, directBumps and computedLabelSet were assigned but never read — removed during merge lint fix
Rewritten to create date-based staging tags (staging-YYYYMMDD-release-N) from main HEAD with sequential counter per date; removed release_tag input
Updated tag trigger to staging-*, triple-tags Docker images (component version + latest-staging + deploy tag), adds API_VERSION/TEE_VERSION to .env.staging
Creates 61 GitHub labels — must use bash 3.2 compatible syntax (no declare -A associative arrays) for macOS compatibility

workflow: Executor subagents run in isolated git worktrees branched from main, not from the feature branch — worktree commits must be cherry-picked onto the feature branch, not merged
lint-staged's stash-restore cycle during pre-commit hooks clobbers in-flight file edits — must re-stage after making lint fixes
529 API throttling caused ~25 min of dead time on wave 1 (43 min wall clock vs 4 min actual work); wave 2 was much faster (~4 min wall clock)
The GSD orchestrator's working directory can drift into a worktree path if bash is run from that context — always verify cwd before git operations
Merging worktree branches with 'git merge' returns 'Already up to date' when the worktree branched from main and the feature branch has diverged — cherry-pick is the correct approach
Conventional commit format is required by pre-commit hooks — merge commits with non-conventional messages will be rejected
STATE.md performance metrics table had a format mismatch: rows 39-81 used 5-column format while newer rows used 4-column Phase XX PYY format

friction: 529 API overload errors caused ~25 minutes of retry backoff during Wave 1 execution
Executor worktrees branch from main, not the feature branch — this was not anticipated and required cherry-picking instead of merging
lint-staged stash-restore cycle silently clobbered file edits during commit attempts, causing multiple failed commit attempts before the root cause was identified
The orchestrator's cwd drifted into a worktree directory, causing git commands to operate on the wrong repo context
STATE.md had merge conflicts on every cherry-pick due to all three agents independently updating it
Dead code in the agent-generated pr-release-preview.js (maxBump, directBumps, computedLabelSet) triggered eslint failures that blocked the merge commit
